what: You listen to a discussion between a few people. Then you speak to summarize the main points and each person's view.
tests: Listening and speaking: following several speakers and summarizing the discussion.

scoring.note: Pearson's page lists these scored traits.

strategy: Note the topic, then one key point for each speaker (their name or first letter helps).
Note any agreement, disagreement or final decision.
Organise your answer: topic, each view, how the discussion ended.
Use reporting words: suggested, argued, agreed, was worried that.
example_prompt: Three students discuss whether their class should move to online quizzes: one likes the speed, one worries about cheating, one suggests short quizzes in class on laptops.

strong.answer: The students discussed moving their quizzes online. The first student liked how quickly results would come back. The second was worried that people could cheat at home. The third suggested a compromise: short online quizzes taken in class on laptops, so they keep the speed and reduce cheating.
strong.why: It covers the topic, every speaker's view and the final idea, using reporting language.

medium.answer: They talked about online quizzes. One said it is fast. Another said cheating. Then they decided something about laptops.
medium.why: Main points are partly there, but the solution is unclear.

weak.answer: It was a discussion about school and the students had different opinions about it.
weak.why: No specific points from the discussion.

mistakes: Retelling every sentence instead of the main ideas.
